source: (1) Michael Hill (LeadDev Managing Editor), 'The struggle to prove AI productivity gains', LeadDev, 25 March 2026. Opened in full: https://leaddev.com/ai/the-struggle-to-prove-ai-productivity-gains. Note: the article is by Michael Hill and reports on Multitudes; it is not authored by Multitudes. (2) Primary: Lauren Peate and Youxiang Lei, Multitudes, 'What matters most for embedding AI: How you adapt' (AI Impact Whitepaper 2, March 2026), 32-page PDF opened in full via https://www.multitudes.com/what-matters-most-for-embedding-ai-how-you-adapt (PDF: cdn.prod.website-files.com/.../AI Impact Whitepaper 2 - March 2026.pdf). (3) Also opened for the out-of-hours claim: Multitudes, 'What matters most for AI rollouts: How you lead' (Whitepaper 1), linked from https://www.multitudes.com/data-to-cut-through-the-hype.
data_type: Survey plus interviews (whitepaper 2: two surveys and 29 interviews; free-text answers coded with LLM-assisted thematic analysis reviewed by humans). Whitepaper 1 adds telemetry (500+ developers at 4 organisations). LeadDev piece is journalism with expert quotes.
sample_and_method: Whitepaper 2: 'Our survey dataset has 428 responses' (54% ICs, 46% leaders; 45% from orgs with 250+ engineers, 34% 20-249, 21% 1-19). Phase 1 deep-dive: 202 survey responses from four organisations, July-October 2025, plus 19 interviews Aug-Oct 2025. Phase 2 industry survey: 226 responses, October 2025-February 2026, plus 10 interviews March 2026. Overall programme: '500+ individual contributors (ICs) and 200+ engineering leaders' over 15 months (Jan 2025-Mar 2026). Organisations were a mix of Multitudes customers and non-customers (per the whitepaper 1 landing page). Recruitment method for the industry survey is not described beyond 'hundreds of organizations'. Crucially, the OKR and board-pressure figures come from the 226-response industry survey with small chart bases: outcomes wanted N=203; OKR metrics N=63; hard-to-measure N=47 (respondents with OKRs); board pressures N=75 leaders; managing pressures N=45 leaders. LeadDev's 'more than 700 engineering professionals' does not match the whitepaper's 428 survey responses (it appears to sum 500+ ICs and 200+ leaders across the whole programme).
vendor_interest: Yes. Multitudes is an 'engineering intelligence platform' that sells an 'AI impact feature' and an AI ROI calculator; the whitepaper pages carry a customer case study (Eucalyptus). LeadDev is a media and events company.
headline_figures: Whitepaper 2: 'Only 31% reported having AI-related OKRs. As one VP of Engineering told us bluntly when asked about AI metrics: "I don't have any good ones."'

Whitepaper 2: 'Among those who did have AI OKRs, the most common metrics were activity-focused rather than outcome-based: 71% tracked AI feature delivery and 71% tracked AI adoption rates, while only 44% measured velocity and 37% measured speed (Figure 7).' (N = 63)
Whitepaper 2: 'The results were remarkably aligned: 86% want to move faster, 86% want to reduce tedious work, and 64% want to deliver more features (Figure 6).' (engineering leaders, N = 203)
Whitepaper 2: 'Even though 86% of respondents said they wanted to move faster, only 15% had OKRs related to speed and velocity in place to track whether that was actually happening.'

Whitepaper 2: 'Of the respondents with OKRs, 75% had something that they found hard to measure about the impact of AI. The most common challenges were with measuring productivity (26%), capturing human impact (19%), and isolating AI's contribution from other factors (15%) (Figure 8).' (N = 47)
Whitepaper 2: '55% of all industry survey respondents said they were facing pressure from the board regarding AI.'

Whitepaper 2: 'When we asked leaders what those pressures looked like (Figure 9), the top response was around AI adoption (40%) ... But the second-highest was expectations for improved outcomes (39%) ... Among those citing outcome expectations, the vast majority (60%) named productivity as the desired result.' (N = 75 leaders)

Whitepaper 2: 'Investing more resources and effort into AI learning & development (22%); Transparently communicating both the good and bad (18%); Resetting board expectations via education (18%)' (N = 45 leaders)

LeadDev (secondary): 'Multitudes carried out a study of more than 700 engineering professionals and found that 75% of participants struggle to measure AI's impact.' [uncertain: overstated; see caveats]

LeadDev (secondary, LeadDev's own research): 'According to the AI Impact Report 2025, 98% of respondents are exploring the use of AI tools and models, yet the most common challenge for 60% of respondents is a lack of clear metrics to evaluate their impact.' [uncertain: LeadDev AI Impact Report 2025 not opened]
Whitepaper 1: 'Engineers merged 27.2% more PRs with AI – but did 19.6% more out-of-hours commits.'
metric_layer: Measures what organisations track. Finding: AI OKRs, where they exist, sit at the input/usage and activity layers (AI adoption rates 71%, AI feature delivery 71%) more than delivery (velocity 44%, speed 37%). Desired outcomes are delivery and developer-experience goals (move faster, reduce tedious work, more features). Board pressure is mostly adoption (input layer) shifting toward outcomes, mainly productivity. Financial outcome ('Demonstrating ROI') appears only as a small theme in Figure 9 (value not stated in text). Whitepaper 1 measures delivery (merge frequency) and wellbeing (out-of-hours commits) from telemetry.
respondent_role_split: Partial. Sample split 54% ICs, 46% leaders. Board-pressure and managing-pressure questions were asked of leaders only (N = 75 and N = 45). Desired-outcomes question was asked of engineering leaders (N = 203 of 226). Leaders are defined as 'Managers of ICs, Engineering Managers, Directors, Vice Presidents, and Executive or C-suite roles'; no split by manager vs director vs executive for the measurement figures. One IC/leader split elsewhere: ICs '4.7x more likely to cite lack of tool availability as a barrier (14% of ICs vs 3% of leaders)'.
workload_signal: Board pressure for productivity gains: one CTO quote, '[The board expects] a 50% productivity improvement across my team, but I'm not going to get that – so I need a quantification of what I am getting right now.' Whitepaper 1 telemetry: 'a 19.6% increase in out-of-hours commits. This means that developers were doing more work in evenings and weekends than they did before the AI rollout... It could be that 19.6% of the merge frequency increase is just from longer hours, which would leave just 7.6 percentage points of change that could be explained by the AI tooling itself.' Multitudes stresses these are 'relational rather than causal'. LeadDev paraphrases Peate: 'AI rollouts are bringing more out-of-hours work, so teams should track this as an indicator of the human impact.'
definition_of_value_offered: Yes. Whitepaper 2 recommendations: choose good-enough metrics tied to the 'why' for AI; 'Done is better than perfect: Choose good-enough metrics, and then focus on trends over time. Looking at the change in metrics before versus after interventions is also a good way to tease out the impact of your actions instead of confounding factors'; 'Boards are starting to shift their focus from AI adoption to AI outcomes – get ahead by looking at outcome metrics now'; use metrics to manage up. Suggests change lead time (move faster), developer experience (reduce tedious work) and velocity (more features) as matching metrics. In LeadDev, Peate names four buckets: 'AI usage data, customer value delivered, customer pain created, and the impact on human engineers' (tokens, lines accepted, cost, intervention dates; features or fallback PRs/tickets; incidents and bug reports with leading indicators; out-of-hours work). LinkedIn's Krishnan Sridhar: 'Ultimately, the most important question is whether teams are delivering on their roadmaps faster and with confidence.'
removal_counterfactual: None directly. The nearest is Whitepaper 1's before/after comparison around AI rollouts (27.2% more PRs merged, 19.6% more out-of-hours commits), which Multitudes says is relational, not causal. LeadDev mentions comparing high vs low AI adopters and before/after experiments as methods, not results.
key_quotes: "[The board expects] a 50% productivity improvement across my team, but I'm not going to get that – so I need a quantification of what I am getting right now." (CTO, Multitudes whitepaper 2)
"Before, they wanted to know we were doing something. What it's started to turn into is the expectation of something coming out the other side." (CTO, Multitudes whitepaper 2)
caveats: Vendor research (Multitudes sells AI impact measurement). LeadDev's write-up misstates several figures relative to the primary: (a) 'more than 700 engineering professionals' vs 428 survey responses; (b) '75% of participants struggle to measure AI's impact' vs 75% of respondents WITH OKRs (N = 47) having something hard to measure; (c) '40% of participants feel board-level pressure just to adopt' and '39%... improvement outcomes' are shares of 75 leaders who described pressures, while 55% of all industry respondents reported any board pressure; (d) 'cited by 26% of Multitude's respondents' is 26% of N = 47. LeadDev's tech debt (13%) and quality of outputs (11%) and 'push back (7%) or define usage policies (4%)' come from charts whose values are not stated in the PDF text, so they are [uncertain]. Self-report survey with small sub-bases; free-text answers coded with LLM assistance. Industry survey recruitment not described. Out-of-hours finding is correlational.
access: LeadDev article opened in full. Multitudes Whitepaper 2 PDF (32 pages) opened in full as text; chart bar values not visible as text, so only figures stated in prose are used. Whitepaper 1 PDF opened and searched for the out-of-hours passage only (not read end to end). Not opened: LeadDev AI Impact Report 2025 (the 98%/60% figures).
